doc.title: Peter Appleyard interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 4, 2012

title: Toots Thielemans, Emil Richards, and a failed audition for George Shearing
summary: Appleyard was tried out for Shearing's group, asked to scat a phrase he could not play, and did not get the job.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: The Shearing thing. And you asked me did a guitar player help me? Toots was with him then — Toots Thielemans.

And he was awfully kind to me because a vibraphone player, Johnny Ray, was leaving. And so he said, “What is your vote on George?” I said, “I don’t know.” Because prior to Johnny, a vibraphone player being with him — I’m just trying to think of his name — and George wasn’t too generous in those days as regards to them playing. He would give them eight bars here and eight bars there you know, that kind of thing. So this guy came for my dinner this night, to my house for dinner, and he said, “Wait ‘till I get to the gig tonight, I’m going to screw George.” He said, “We’re going to do ‘Jordu,’” we always play it, to start off.” And he said, “I’m going to take six choruses.” And George is doing this you know. And he became the biggest percussionist in Hollywood, oh, and made a fortune.
I’ll be darned. © Fillius Jazz Archive -13-

But I hadn’t seen him in all those years. Anyway, they put me in front of George and George said, “Can you do this?” And he went [scats frenetically]. I said, “No I can’t do that.” And Emil said, “That’s too bad you can’t do that because he won’t hire a guy if he can’t do that.
